class_declaration:
# Each object is the one color-2 cell in the grid. The output replaces it with its 4 diagonal neighbors in fixed colors, 3 top left, 6 top right, 8 bottom left, 7 bottom right, leaving out any that fall outside the grid
class Obj(x: int, y: int, width: int, height: int, orientation: int, volume: int, tag: str = 'l7544'):
    this.x is x
    this.y is y
    this.width is width
    this.height is height
    this.orientation is orientation
    this.volume is volume
    this.tag is tag
declarations:
# Each cell becomes l2898, the four corners of a 3x3 box around it, its center left empty
$Obj.tag is l2898

# Corner colors, top row then bottom row: 3 and 6 above, 8 and 7 below
$Obj.corner_colors is [[3, 6], [8, 7]]

# Leftmost corner column that lies inside the grid
$Obj.x is min of [$Obj.x@first - 1, $Obj.x@first + 1].filter(column => column >= 0 and column < canvas_width)

# Top corner row that lies inside the grid
$Obj.y is min of [$Obj.y@first - 1, $Obj.y@first + 1].filter(row => row >= 0 and row < canvas_height)

# Columns from the leftmost to the rightmost corner inside the grid
$Obj.width is max of [$Obj.x@first - 1, $Obj.x@first + 1].filter(column => column >= 0 and column < canvas_width) - $Obj.x + 1

# Rows from the top to the bottom corner inside the grid
$Obj.height is max of [$Obj.y@first - 1, $Obj.y@first + 1].filter(row => row >= 0 and row < canvas_height) - $Obj.y + 1

# Number of corners inside the grid
$Obj.volume is [$Obj.x@first - 1, $Obj.x@first + 1].filter(column => column >= 0 and column < canvas_width).length * [$Obj.y@first - 1, $Obj.y@first + 1].filter(row => row >= 0 and row < canvas_height).length
